text:
India’s renewable energy opportunity is now shifting from pure capacity addition to execution scale… and one small-cap player which is quietly building a serious Wind + Hybrid infrastructure platform is KP Energy 

In just 4 years, the company has scaled from ₹254 Cr revenue in FY22 to ₹1,506 Cr in FY26 - nearly a 6x jump while maintaining profitability and improving margins.

FY26 performance remained exceptionally strong:

• Revenue up 57% YoY to ₹1,506 Cr
• EBITDA surged 68% YoY to ₹328 Cr
• PAT grew 57% YoY to ₹181 Cr
• Q4 FY26 PAT jumped 72% YoY to ₹79 Cr
• EBITDA margin expanded to 22%

But the bigger story is how the company is scaling.
KP Energy is gradually evolving from a regional wind EPC contractor into an integrated renewable infrastructure platform with presence across:
• Wind EPC
• Hybrid renewable projects
• O&M services
• IPP assets
• Power evacuation infrastructure

This diversification is important because it reduces dependence on pure EPC execution and creates multiple monetisation layers across the renewable value chain. 

Operational scale is also becoming meaningful:

• 646+ MW O&M portfolio
• 200 MW IPP assets under execution
• Targeting 10+ GW portfolio by 2030

One important technology milestone:
KP Energy became the first company in India to install Senvion’s “Make in India” 4.2M160 wind turbine in South Gujarat — reflecting strong execution capability and adaptability toward next-generation turbine platforms. 

Another major development:
The company recently received Inter-State Electricity Trading Licence from CERC, allowing participation in pan-India power markets and potentially opening new monetisation opportunities beyond traditional EPC revenues. 

Order inflows also remain healthy:
• 100 MW ISTS-connected wind project from SECI
• 99 MW wind EPC project from Inox Renewable
• 91.4 MW hybrid project from JK Paper
• 40.8 MW hybrid project from Enerparc

Key strengths:

• Strong execution-led scaling
• Margin expansion despite rapid growth
• Increasing hybrid + IPP exposure
• Beneficiary of India’s renewable capacity push
• Expanding beyond regional concentration

Key risks:

• EPC businesses inherently carry high working capital intensity
• Renewable tendering/policy delays can impact execution timelines
• Aggressive scaling requires disciplined capital allocation and balance sheet management

KP Energy still operates in a relatively undertracked segment of the market but the company increasingly looks less like a regional wind EPC player and more like an integrated renewable infrastructure platform being built for long-term scale.

- A strong pipeline of contracts in Reliance’s large‑scale projects, including EPC, BESS, hybrid plants, and hydrogen‑related infrastructure.

Craftsman Automation Q4 FY26.

Q4 Revenue: ₹2,226 cr · +27.3% YoY 
Q4 EBITDA margin: 16.1% · +218 bps YoY 
FY26 Revenue: ₹8,069 cr · +41.8% YoY, beat ₹7,000 cr guidance by 15% 
FY26 Normalised PAT: ₹393 cr · +84.2% YoY

Three guidance beats in a row. One significant miss.

Revenue, EBITDA, EBIT all beat guidance. Cleanly.

FY26 EBITDA: ₹1,239 cr vs ₹1,100 cr guided (+13%). Revenue: ₹8,069 cr vs ₹7,000 cr guided (+15%). All three segment EBIT margins expanded YoY in Q4, Powertrain by 600 bps to 19.2%, Aluminium by 140 bps to 10.2%, Industrial by 50 bps to 6.1%. CFO grew 84% YoY to ₹522 cr, CFO/PAT at 1.36x, the earnings are converting to cash.

Aluminium Products is 59% of revenue and grew 57.9% YoY for the full year. That is the volume engine. 

Powertrain at 19.2% EBIT margin is the profitability engine.

The capex overshoot is the number that matters for FY27.

Group capex guidance: ₹750–800 cr. Actual: ₹1,188 cr. A 50% overshoot. Management cited capacity constraints preventing the company from bidding on large orders, the capex was demand-justified, not reckless. But the consequence is real: Net Debt/EBITDA at 2.55x versus a <2.0x target, FCF at −₹667 cr, and total borrowings up 48% YoY.

The capacity is now being built. The question for FY27 is whether it converts to revenue before leverage becomes uncomfortable.

One flag: warranty and rejection provisions nearly tripled YoY to ₹11 cr from ₹4 cr. Small in absolute terms, but worth monitoring as the business scales rapidly.

Note : This is not an investment advise.

text:
Monolithisch India Ltd Q4 FY26 → Management guiding for 100%+ growth ahead 

Monolithisch India is steadily transforming from a traditional ramming mass manufacturer into a premium, scale-driven industry leader backed by strong industry tailwinds, capacity expansion & improving product mix.

 FY26 Performance Highlights
• Revenue: ₹135.3 Cr (+48% YoY)
• EBITDA: ₹31.5 Cr (+68% YoY)
• PAT: ₹23 Cr (+72% YoY)
• ROC remained strong at ~46%

Q4 FY26 was another standout quarter:
• Revenue: ₹40.6 Cr (+35% YoY)
• EBITDA: ₹11.4 Cr (+52% YoY)
• PAT: ₹8.1 Cr (+81% YoY)
• EBITDA Margin expanded to ~28%

Premiumisation Strategy Playing Out

The company is moving beyond commoditized premix products toward premium/high-performance grades.
Its “SGB Limited” grade offering with 52–55 hours heat assurance is expected to become a major margin driver, with management targeting ~60% customer migration in Q1 FY27 itself.

This shift can materially improve realizations, margins & customer stickiness over time.

Strong Industry Tailwinds

India’s steel capacity target of 300 MT by FY31 and rising induction furnace (IF) adoption create a strong long-term demand environment for ramming mass.
Since every ton of IF steel requires ramming mass, Monolith stands directly leveraged to this structural industry growth.

The company is strategically positioned in Eastern India — the country’s largest IF hub — giving it strong logistical & customer advantages.

Competitive Advantages

• 99% premix portfolio ensures consistency & lower customer-side errors
• Strong linkage to silica mines/raw material ecosystem
• Strategic proximity to steel clusters improves efficiency & delivery
• Industry consolidation could favour organized players like Monolith

Next Leg of Growth = Capacity Expansion

The upcoming Metalurgica plant in West Bengal is expected to become the world’s largest single-campus ramming mass facility.

Total capacity is expected to increase to ~5.76 lakh MTPA, with commercialization targeted in Q2 FY27.

This expansion can significantly enhance scale benefits & operating leverage over the next few years.

Balance Sheet & Working Capital

• Debt-free balance sheet remains a major strength
• Receivable cycle improved to ~50–60 days
• Higher inventory is being strategically maintained to manage supply disruptions & ensure uninterrupted servicing

FY27 Guidance

Management is guiding for:
• Revenue: ₹250–300 Cr
• EBITDA Margin: 22–25%

If executed well, this implies another phase of sharp earnings growth ahead.

Bottomline

Monolith India is no longer just a volume-driven ramming mass player. Premiumisation, aggressive capacity expansion, strong industry tailwinds, operational efficiencies & a debt-free balance sheet together position the company for potentially strong long-term compounding.

Oswal Pumps Ltd secures an order valued at ₹162.06 crore from Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL) for 6,896 off-grid solar photovoltaic water pumping systems under the PM KUSUM B scheme, to be executed within one year.

Key Highlights:

Order Details:
- Total order value: ₹162.06 crore (inclusive of GST).
- Number of systems: 6,896 off-grid DC solar photovoltaic water pumping systems.
- Capacities of systems: 3 hp, 5 hp, and 7.5 hp.

Execution Timeline:
- Installation to be completed within 60 days from the issuance of the Notice to Proceed (NTP)/work order.
- Letter of empanelment valid for 1 year.

Scope of Work:
- Includes design, manufacture, supply, transport, installation, testing, and commissioning of solar water pumping systems.
- Complete system warranty and repair, maintenance, and remote monitoring system (RMS) for 5 years.

Promoter Interest:
- No interest from promoter/promoter group/group companies in the awarding entity.

Mr. Vivek Gupta, Chairman and Managing Director, Oswal Pumps Limited, stated, “We are pleased to receive yet another order from Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited under the 'Magel Tyala Saur Krishi Pump' yojna."

This order reinforces Oswal Pumps' commitment to sustainable agriculture and renewable energy adoption. 🌱

text:
From Land to Cloud: How a Data Centre Is Built

Data Centre Chain

Land → Building → Power → Cooling → Servers → Network → Software → Cloud

Land & Power : A physical location with access to strong electricity and internet backbone
Think of it like farmland

Building (Shell) : The structure that houses everything, floors, walls, security
Like a warehouse or factory building

Power Infrastructure : Transformers, UPS, batteries, generators ensuring 24/7 electricity
Like irrigation and backup water for crops

Cooling Systems : Keeps machines from overheating (AC, liquid cooling)
Like ventilation and climate control in a greenhouse

Servers (Hardware) : Physical machines that store and process data
Like machines inside a factory doing the work

Networking (Fiber & Switches) : Connects servers to each other and to the internet
Like roads connecting factories to cities

Software & Virtualization : Turns hardware into usable computing (cloud, storage, apps)
Like turning raw factory output into finished goods

Cloud Services : What users actually consume—apps, storage, AI, websites
Like packaged products delivered to customers

Punjab National Bank(PNB) - Q4 FY26 Result Analysis

Q4 PPOP: ₹7,521 cr · +9.2% YoY 
Q4 PAT: ₹5,225 cr · +12.5% YoY 
FY26 Normalised PAT: ₹18,918 cr · +13.8% YoY
FY26 Reported PAT: ₹16,904 cr · +1.7% YoY

The gap between reported and normalised is a ₹3,324 cr one-time DTA charge from switching to the new tax regime. It's non-cash, it won't recur, and it is the primary reason reported PAT growth looks muted. The underlying business grew 13.8%.

The asset quality story is the headline.

GNPA: 2.95% · guided <3% · met. NNPA: 0.29% · guided 0.35% · exceeded. PCR: 97.14%, one of the highest in PSU banking.

These numbers matter structurally. A bank with GNPA under 3% and near-full provision coverage has largely finished the cleanup cycle. Future credit costs have significantly less room to surprise negatively. Floating provisions were also increased by ₹1,295 cr during FY26 to ₹2,045 cr, a proactive buffer being built ahead of the ECL regime transition.

The NII miss is the key concern. It's real and it's not small.

FY26 NII: ₹41,960 cr · -1.9% YoY · guided +7%. That is an 890 bps miss on the most important income line for a bank. Interest expended grew 9.1% while interest earned grew only 5.5%. The math is simple, funding costs rose faster than asset yields, and net interest margins compressed.

Consequently, ROA came in at 0.89% for the year, missing the >1% target. PPOP grew only because opex fell sharply, employee costs dropped 34.8% YoY in Q4, likely due to a high base from wage revision provisions in Q4 FY25. That opex relief is not repeatable at the same scale.

Loan growth and capital are genuinely strong.

Advances grew 13.7% YoY to ₹12.25 lakh crore, beating the 11–12% guidance. CAR at 17.74%, CET1 at 13.62%, net worth +21.4% YoY. The balance sheet has the capacity to grow. CFO: ₹25,635 cr, up 16.1% YoY, CFO/PAT at 1.5x, the earnings are converting to cash cleanly.

Q4 segment breakdown: Corporate/Wholesale PBT +28.8% YoY, Retail +16.7% YoY. Treasury was the drag at -26.0% YoY, likely MTM losses in a volatile rate environment.

FY27 is a NIM recovery story, or it isn't.

The bank has done the hard work on asset quality. Growth metrics are strong. The one open question is whether the rate environment allows NII to recover. If the repo rate eases in FY27 and cost of deposits reprices faster than asset yields compress, NIM expands and ROA crosses 1%. If rates stay sticky, NII remains under pressure and the ROA miss persists.

That binary is what FY27 results will answer.

Note : This is not an investment advise.

💥IRGC STRIKES THE UAE'S BYPASS HUB‼️

In a dramatic escalation of Middle East tensions, Iranian drones struck the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone in the UAE today, May 4, 2026, sparking MASSIVE fires & forcing immediate suspension of key operations at one of the world’s most critical oil export and storage facilities.

This targeted attack is poised to DRASTICALLY worsen global oil supplies, driving prices sharply higher & sending shockwaves through energy markets already on edge.

Fujairah, situated on the Gulf of Oman, serves as the UAE’s vital Hormuz-bypass hub. 
It handles roughly 1.7 million barrels per day of crude exports and refined products-equivalent to about 1.7% of global daily demand-along with massive storage capacity exceeding 100 million barrels. 

As a primary outlet for ADNOC’s Murban crude and a major bunkering center, any sustained disruption here removes meaningful volumes from the market at a precarious time. 

Loading operations have already been halted as a precaution, and damage assessments suggest repairs could take weeks or longer amid heightened security risks.

The impact will be immediate & severe. 
With tanker insurance premiums surging and shipping routes under threat, effective global supply could tighten by millions of barrels daily. 

Oil prices, already trading well above $105 per barrel, are expected to rocket higher-potentially reaching $130–$150 in the near term-as traders price in prolonged outages and fears of broader regional escalation. 

This is no minor incident; it signals Iran’s readiness to strike energy infrastructure directly, compounding existing pressures from the ongoing conflict.

The fallout extends far beyond the pump. 
Skyrocketing energy costs will cascade through the global economy, hitting transportation, manufacturing, and agriculture hardest. 

Food prices are set to rise dramatically: diesel for tractors and trucks, natural gas-derived fertilizers, and petroleum-based pesticides will all become far more expensive. 

Global supply chains-already stretched-will face higher logistics costs, leading to reduced food availability, empty shelves in import-dependent regions across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East, and accelerated food inflation. 
For millions already struggling with high living costs, this could mean genuine shortages and heightened risk of social unrest.

Today’s strike on Fujairah is a game-changer. 
It not only threatens energy security but also guarantees higher prices at the gas station and grocery store alike, underscoring how geopolitical flashpoints can rapidly erode both oil supplies and everyday affordability worldwide. 

Markets should brace for a new era of energy-driven inflation.
